title_as_printed: Apparent molar heat capacity Cp,phi of CO2(aq) where cp,s and cp,w denote the massic heat capacity of the solution and pure water, respectively
property_note: apparent molar heat capacity of the dissolved gas CO2 in pure water (no salt), Cp,phi = M2 cp,s + (cp,s - cp,w)/m (eq 1), cp,w from Hill's equation of state; the authors use Cp,phi at the lowest molality as an approximation to the partial molar heat capacity Cp,m,2
pressure_note: flow calorimeter; p printed per row (about 28 MPa, 27.95 to 28.04 MPa); single liquid phase

T.note: average of the temperatures before and after heating; uncertainty 0.05 K below 600 K, 0.2 K above, up to 0.7 K between 658 and 678 K

value.what: apparent molar heat capacity of CO2(aq) from eq (1)

value2.what: measured ratio of massic heat capacity of solution to pure water at the same T and p (average of two or more experiments)

m_gas.what: molality of CO2 (mol per kg water)

notes: Molality uncertainty (0.7, 0.5, 0.5, 0.3) per cent for CH4, CO2, H2S, NH3. Cp,phi uncertainty about 1 per cent below 623 K, rising to about 25 per cent of the peak value near the critical region. Ionization corrections ignored by the authors (small; largest for NH3 at 303 K).
